note: Three industry associations (IFAC/CBA/PCAC) barred financial+payment institutions from crypto services; superseded by the comprehensive ban Sep 24;conf=high
Comprehensive ban: PBOC + 9 agencies declared all crypto transactions illegal financial activity (H6 event date);conf=high
CBN letter barred banks/OFIs from servicing crypto; lifted by CBN VASP Guidelines 2023-12-22 (holding/trading never criminalised);conf=high
RBI circular barred banks from servicing crypto; struck down by Supreme Court 2020-03-04 (IAMAI v RBI). Only the lift is in-sample;conf=high
CBRT regulation (Official Gazette 2021-04-16, effective 2021-04-30) banned crypto as means of payment; holding/trading remain legal;conf=high
SBP BPRD/FE Circular 03 of 2018 barred financial institutions from crypto; reversed 2026-04-14 (BPRD Circular 10/2026) which is out of sample, so open within window;conf=high
Bank Indonesia prohibited crypto as means of payment (2017 PBI / Jan-2018 enforcement); trading legal as a commodity via Bappebti (2019). Date approx to Jan-1;conf=med
State Bank of Vietnam: issuance/supply/use of crypto as means of payment prohibited from 2018-01-01 (admin fines); holding/trading not criminalised. Corrects YAML absolute flag;conf=high
Law No.259-FZ (Digital Financial Assets) effective 2021-01-01 legalises crypto but bans its use as payment for domestic goods/services;conf=high
Office des Changes + Bank Al-Maghrib + MEF joint statement Nov-2017 declared crypto transactions illegal under FX law; still in force (draft legalisation pending 2025). Day approximate;conf=med
2018 Finance Law (Law 17-11) Article 117 prohibits purchase/sale/use/possession of virtual currency; in force 2018-01-01;conf=high

Central Bank & Banking Law No.194 of 2020 prohibits issuing/trading/promoting crypto without CBE licence (CBE warning earlier in 2018; Dar al-Ifta fatwa 2018). Using 2020 law as binding date; day approximate;conf=med
Central Bank of Tunisia: crypto dealing illegal without state authorisation under the FX code (May-2018 statement); penalties incl. imprisonment; still in force. Day approximate;conf=med
Bangladesh Bank notice (2017) declares crypto transactions illegal under Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 / AML / Anti-Terrorism acts; still in force. Day approximate;conf=med
Qatar Central Bank Feb-2018 circular barred banks from crypto dealing; superseded by QFCRA absolute prohibition Jan-2020. Day approximate;conf=med
QFCRA 2020 prohibition: no virtual-asset service in/from the QFC (fiat-crypto, crypto-crypto, custody). LoC 2021 classes Qatar absolute. Day approximate;conf=med
Standing committee (incl. SAMA/CMA) 2018 declared virtual currencies illegal/unlicensed; banks barred from crypto without SAMA approval; holding not criminalised. Day approximate;conf=med

CMA Circular 10/2023 + CBK: 'absolute prohibition' on crypto payments, investment and mining (2023-07-17). Coded absolute given breadth; holding-only not explicitly criminalised so could be payment. Within-sample transition;conf=med
Banque du Liban / CMA 2018 prohibit licensed financial institutions from crypto activity (building on 2013 BDL warning); P2P not enforced. Holding not criminalised. Day approximate;conf=low
Bank of Tanzania Nov-2019 public notice: crypto not recognised, banks/FIs barred; reversal discussed since 2022 but not formally rescinded in-window. Day approximate;conf=med
Bank of Namibia 2018 stance: crypto not legal tender, exchanges/banking barred; Virtual Assets Act 2023 (assented Jul-2023) replaced the ban with licensing. Dates approximate;conf=low

Central Bank of Jordan 2014 circular barred banks/FIs from crypto (reinforced 2018, 2019); replaced by Virtual Assets Transactions Regulation Law in 2025 (lift date within 2025 uncertain, left open). Corrects YAML false. Day approximate;conf=med
